title_en: The Perfect Storm That Clobbered Hedge Funds
title_zh: 重创对冲基金的完美风暴：与 Nishant Kumar、Michael Ball 复盘 10 月
subtitle_zh: 多策略基金集体失守、AI 交易拥挤反噬，Bloomberg 记者与宏观策略师复盘 10 月完美风暴。
summary_zh: 本期 Odd Lots 采用双嘉宾分段形式，Tracy Alloway 与 Joe Weisenthal 先对话 Bloomberg News 对冲基金条线首席记者 Nishant Kumar，再请宏观策略师 Michael Ball 复盘大盘。Kumar 称报道对冲基金 16 年来从没见过上周那样忙的月份：10 月对多策略基金（multi-strats）是一场完美风暴，Millennium、Balyasney、Point72、ExodusPoint 等主流 pod shop 罕见地在同一个月一起亏钱——Millennium 跌 2.3%，看似不大，但对其年化约 14% 的稳健载体已属重创。核心问题是相关性（correlation）：这些本该分散、独立下注的 pod，过去 12 到 24 个月几乎都在隐性加杠杆做多 AI，引用 PivotalPath 报告显示大家挤在同样的股票上；节目也重提 Krishna Kumar 的观点——多策略基金最大化的是短期而非长期回报。Ball 随后解释周四的系统性抛售：波动率控制（vol control）、系统化交易者与 CTA 被迫降敞口，跌破横盘数月的区间测试新低，信用市场也喊够了。两人辨析超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）表现不佳源于 Amazon、Microsoft、Google 搜索等传统业务挣扎，以及 neocloud 与算力租户的分散化失灵。结尾点出真正痛点：捐赠基金与养老金天然做多风险资产，为对冲付了钱却在最该起作用的月份没得到对冲。
description: The Perfect Storm That Clobbered Hedge Funds

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios.
turns.zh: Bloomberg Audio Studios。

turns.en: Podcasts. Radio. News.
turns.zh: 播客、广播、新闻。

turns.en: Hello and welcome to another episode of the OddLots Podcast.
turns.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听新一期的 OddLots 播客。

turns.en: I'm Tracy Alloway.
turns.zh: 我是 Tracy Alloway。

turns.en: And I'm Joe Wiesenthal.
turns.zh: 我是 Joe Weisenthal。

turns.en: Joe, I heard with all the market volatility recently.
turns.zh: Joe，我听说最近市场波动这么大——

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: I heard a pod is blowing up.
turns.zh: 我听说有个 pod 要爆仓了。

turns.en: You heard a rumor.
turns.zh: 你听到传言了。

turns.en: I heard a rumor.
turns.zh: 我听到传言了。

turns.en: Is that something being said? Anyone here? Anyone hearing talk of a pod blowing up?
turns.zh: 真有人在这么说吗？在场的谁听到"哪个 pod 要爆"的传闻了吗？

turns.en: Somewhere a pod is always blowing up. No, but I think actually the past week or so for a lot of hedge funds has been kind of historic.
turns.zh: 总有某个地方的 pod 在爆仓嘛。不过说真的，我觉得过去这一周左右，对很多对冲基金来说，可以说是历史性的。

turns.en: So I would say October, just from the numbers that we've already got in, awful. And I would say it was this drip. There's been weakness in a lot of the popular AI adjacent names really since the middle of the summer. But it's building and building. Already getting kind of ugly. And then maybe with the midterms or something, you get this huge washout. And yeah, big numbers, big losses.
turns.zh: 光是从我们已经拿到的数据看，我会说 10 月非常糟糕。整个过程像是持续渗漏——从夏天中段开始，很多热门的 AI 相关标的就一直在走弱，跌势不断累积，本来就已经有点难看了。然后可能碰上中期选举之类的，你就看到一次巨大的洗盘。是的，数字很大，亏损也很大。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: So we're recording this on November 10th. And I say the past week because that's when we got all the headlines about October performance for a lot of these funds. But for multi-strats in particular, I mean, we've done a lot of episodes on these. These were the hot new funds. They were supposed to be able to manage money in up and down markets instead of relying on like, one star investor or one centralized team. You had all these little pods that were supposed to be making bets independent of each other, uncorrelated. Correlation, as I always say, is one of the trickiest concepts on Wall Street to actually model. And so it looks like there are some questions about the business model. Did everyone basically pile into the same trade?
turns.zh: 我们这期是在 11 月 10 日录的。我说"过去一周"，是因为那正是我们收到一大批基金 10 月业绩头条的时间。但对多策略基金（multi-strats）来说，我们做过很多期节目聊它们。它们曾是那种最当红的新基金，理应在上涨和下跌的市场里都能管钱，而不是靠某一位明星投资人或某一个核心操盘团队。你有一堆小 pod，本来应该各自独立地下注、彼此不相关。相关性（correlation），我一直说，是华尔街最难真正建模的概念之一。所以现在看起来，这个商业模式是有些问题的。大家基本上都挤到了同一笔交易上吗？

turns.en: Implicitly. So this is, I think, the number one question, which is that Could you have made a lot of money in the last 12 or 24 months without implicitly being long AI?
turns.zh: 隐性地。我觉得这是头号问题：在过去 12 到 24 个月里，你能不能在不隐性做多 AI 的前提下赚到很多钱？

turns.en: Was there some other- And probably leveraged on long AI.
turns.zh: 有没有别的——而且大概率还加了杠杆做多 AI。

turns.en: And leveraged long AI. But this is the question. You can dress up the AI trade in a million ways, right? So you could do it through chips. You could even theoretically create exposure to AI through rates, whatever. But at the end of the day, if you were making money over the last year up until recently- were you doing it by implicitly being long AI? And did your boss, the risk manager at your firm, understand that the way you were making money was implicitly long AI, if in fact that's what you were doing?
turns.zh: 而且加了杠杆做多 AI。但问题就在这里。你可以把 AI 交易包装成上百万种样子，对吧？可以通过芯片来做，甚至理论上还能通过利率来构造 AI 敞口，随便什么。但归根结底，如果你在过去一年直到最近一直在赚钱——你是通过隐性做多 AI 赚的吗？你公司里的风控主管、你的老板，是不是明白你赚钱的方式其实就是隐性做多 AI，如果事实真是这样的话？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Basically, we're multi-strats, just momentum dressed up in, I don't know, diversified sheep's clothing. I'm just drawing that metaphor. But I think that is the question. And I'm glad to say we have two very special, perfect guests. We're going to be discussing the hedge fund performance specifically with Nishant Kumar. He is the chief correspondent for hedge funds over at Bloomberg News. And then we're going to have on Michael Ball, who's a macro strategist at Bloomberg News, to talk generally about what's going on in markets, because there's a lot right now. So why don't we go ahead and get started? Nishant, thank you so much for coming on OddLots.
turns.zh: 基本上，我们这些多策略基金，说白了就是披着"分散化羊皮"的动量交易——这比喻是我随口编的。但我觉得问题就在这里。我很高兴我们请到了两位非常特别、非常合适的嘉宾。我们将先和 Nishant Kumar 讨论对冲基金的业绩，他是 Bloomberg News 的对冲基金条线首席记者；然后再请 Michael Ball，他是 Bloomberg News 的宏观策略师，来聊聊市场大盘到底在发生什么，因为眼下事情实在太多。那我们开始吧。Nishant，非常感谢你上 OddLots。

turns.en: Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: Why don't we start with a basic question? You've been pretty busy in recent days. I think you've written dozens of stories at this point. But how bad was October slash early November for a lot of these funds?
turns.zh: 我们先从一个基础问题开始吧。你最近这几天特别忙，我想你已经写了几十条新闻了。但对这些基金来说，10 月加 11 月初到底有多糟？

turns.en: Well, how busy I was in the last 16 years of covering hedge funds, I never saw a day like last week.
turns.zh: 这么说吧，我报道对冲基金 16 年，从没见过哪一天像上周那样忙。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: I just took a screenshot of all my stories and posted on Twitter and it got like 750,000 views. So that tells you how busy it was. But in terms of hedge fund performance, look, it was pretty bad. The interesting bit wasn't just that hedge funds lost money. It was that lots of different strategies got hit at the same time. So coming back to your main point that how correlated some of these strategies have become. Take, for example, Millennium, Ballyasney, 0.72, Exodus Point. These are all the mainstream pot shops that you, although, you know, pots sound like an insult to many of the people in the industry, but that's what they are. And they all lost money together. So these are the hedge funds who have the biggest concentration of assets, biggest concentration of talent, the most sought after hedge funds from investors because they have a track record of making money when the downturn hits. And they all failed together and they lost money last month. Millennium was down 2.3%. Now, on its own, this may not sound like a huge loss, but in their own context, they annualize at around 14%. And when they lose 2.3% in a month, that's a lot for a steady vehicle like Millennium. Same story at Ballyasney, same story at Exodus Point, 0.72. So yeah, I would say it was really bad. Normally, you might see equities had a bad month, but macro did well. or credit go ahead or stock pickers were fine. But this was like a perfect storm. Everyone failed together.
turns.zh: 我刚把自己所有报道截图发到 Twitter 上，大概有 75 万次浏览，你就知道有多忙了。但对冲基金的业绩方面，说实话，非常糟糕。有意思的地方不只是对冲基金亏钱，而是很多不同的策略同时被打击。回到你之前那个观点——这些策略之间已经变得多么相关。举个例子，Millennium、Balyasney、Point72、ExodusPoint，这些都是主流的 pod shop——虽然"pod"这个词在业内很多人听来有点像骂人，但事实就是这样。它们全都在同一个月一起亏钱。这几家对冲基金资产集中度最高、人才集中度最高，也是投资人最追捧的对冲基金，因为它们在下跌来临时历来是能赚钱的。而它们这次全都失守、上个月一起亏钱。Millennium 跌了 2.3%。单看这个数也许不算巨大亏损，但放在它们自己的语境里——它们年化收益大约在 14% 左右——一个月亏 2.3% 对 Millennium 这种稳健载体来说已经很多了。Balyasney 是一样的故事，ExodusPoint、Point72 也是一样的故事。所以是的，我会说真的很糟。平常你可能会看到股票差、宏观好，或者信用债好，或者选股型还行。但这次是一场完美风暴，所有人都一起失守。

turns.en: Wait, can you explain to me why down 2.3% is that bad? I mean, it's bad.
turns.zh: 等等，能不能给我解释一下，为什么跌 2.3% 就算这么糟？我是说，是挺糟的。

turns.en: Well, for a start, it was worse than the S & P 500, right? In October.
turns.zh: 首先，10 月它比 S&P 500 还差，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah, sure. No, yeah, I get that. But like, explain to the listener, and by the listener, I mean me, why 2.3%, which doesn't sound like the end of the world, is, wow, this is one of the craziest months you've ever experienced as a reporter.
turns.zh: 对，是。不，是的，我懂。但请你给听众解释一下——所谓听众，就是我——为什么 2.3% 这个听上去不像世界末日的数字，对你这个记者来说，居然是你经历过最疯狂的月份之一？

turns.en: So as I said, that again, 2.3 in isolation is not bad.
turns.zh: 我刚才说过，2.3% 单看并不糟。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: But you have a specific purpose in a portfolio.
turns.zh: 但你在一个组合里有特定的作用。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: The value of a hedge fund in a pension fund portfolio or a sovereign wealth portfolio, and we are talking about this tens of billions of dollars worth of portfolios. Your role in a portfolio is to soften the blow from any market turmoil. That's the purpose. And you are not expected to match S & P 500 returns when S & P 500 is surging. That's not what is expected from a hedge fund. But when it goes down, when there is a turmoil, investors look at you to protect you. And that's where the problem is.
turns.zh: 对冲基金在养老金组合或者主权财富组合里的价值——我们说的是几百亿美元级别的组合——你在组合里的角色是缓冲任何市场动荡的冲击，这就是目的。当 S&P 500 大涨时，没人指望你追平它的回报，那不是对冲基金该做的事。但当市场下跌、出现动荡时，投资人指望你来保护他们，问题就出在这里。

turns.en: Did anyone, to be fair, it was bad for pretty much every hedge fund out there, but there was at least one I saw that produced positive returns for October, and that was, I think, Citadel. What did they do differently to others? Or what do we think they did differently?
turns.zh: 说句公道话，几乎所有对冲基金这个月都很惨，但至少我看到有一家 10 月是正收益的，我记得是 Citadel。他们和别人做得有什么不一样？或者说我们觉得他们做对了什么？

turns.en: Well, we don't know how, but yes, there were some exceptional winners on the multistrat side. Citadel was one.
turns.zh: 我们不知道具体怎么做到的，但是的，多策略这边确实有几个例外赢家，Citadel 是其中一个。

turns.en: D.U.
turns.zh: D. E.

turns.en: Shaw was another. And there were some odd quant funds that did well. But overall, the picture is still down. Maybe some quants worked out well if someone was shorting heavily. Maybe they were positioned right for last month. But yeah, we don't have portfolio-level details to explain what went right or even what went too wrong at certain hedge funds.
turns.zh: Shaw 是另一个。还有一些奇怪的量化基金表现不错。但整体来看，画面还是下跌的。也许有些量化策略凑效了，如果有人在大量做空，也许他们上个月的仓位刚好对。但整体来说，我们没有组合层面的细节，来解释某些对冲基金究竟做对了什么，或者做错了什么。

turns.en: What's your working, I guess, hypothesis for why everything went wrong for the vast majority of funds?
turns.zh: 你目前大致的工作假设是什么，为什么绝大多数基金的所有事情都出错了？

turns.en: It was a complete mayhem last month. You had AI stocks crashing. You had a surprise election in Brazil. And you have this huge sell-off in the high bond market. And they all combined to create this perfect storm for a lot of different hedge fund industry. You had the French issues and French bonds going down as well.
turns.zh: 上个月完全是混乱。AI 股票崩了；巴西出了一场意外的大选；高收益债市场大幅抛售；再加上法国的问题、法国国债也在跌。所有这些因素叠加，为很多不同的对冲基金造成了这场完美风暴。
所以……

turns.en: There were so many different trades that they were crowded trades and all these hedge funds had piled into them. And one after another, they started to go down. Take, for example, just the AI stocks. We don't know about situational awareness yet, but there is another fund called Alvara.
turns.zh: 有太多不同的交易，全都是拥挤交易，所有对冲基金都挤了进去。然后一个接一个地开始下跌。就拿 AI 股票来说，我们还不知道 Situational Awareness 的情况，但还有另一家基金叫 Alvara。

turns.en: There was a rumor that they were piling back into the market, right? Yeah.
turns.zh: 有传闻说他们在重新加仓，对吧？嗯。

turns.en: Yeah, tell us about this VARA company or this VARA fund. I hadn't heard of it until someone said it was like a situational awareness clone.
turns.zh: 对，跟我们讲讲这家 VARA 公司，或者这家 VARA 基金。我之前从没听说过，直到有人说它像是 Situational Awareness 的翻版。

turns.en: So it was, and we wrote a story that how much of a portfolio overlap there was between VARA and situational awareness. So VARA, for example, lost 33% in October. That's like losing a third of your portfolio. But here's a killer statistic. They are still up for the year. So that's how much money they had made before losing. They had a tough month earlier this year as well. So that's the kind of destruction we are seeing in AI stock. If you are crowded and largely concentrated in a few AI stocks, you take Whale Rock, again, an equity fund down 12%. So there were these highly concentrated single strategies, maybe single market funds, which lost a lot of money. But then if you look at macro hedge funds, they also lost money. Kirkus World, which has like billions and billions of dollars, and they're a macro hedge fund, they lost 6.4%. That was their biggest down month since they started trading. Chris Rokos, another legendary macro hedge fund manager, we just reported today, he lost almost 5% last month. So there was really nowhere to hide in this market. last month.
turns.zh: 它确实是。我们写过一篇报道，讲 VARA 和 Situational Awareness 的持仓重合度有多高。VARA 10 月亏了 33%，等于组合的三分之一没了。但有个惊人的数据——它今年整体仍然是正收益。你就知道在亏损之前他们赚了多少钱。今年早些时候他们也经历过一个艰难的月份。这就是我们在 AI 股票上看到的这种破坏。如果你仓位拥挤、又高度集中在少数几只 AI 股票上——比如 Whale Rock，也是股票型基金，跌了 12%。这类高度集中的单一策略、可能是单一市场基金，亏了很多钱。但如果你再看宏观对冲基金，他们也在亏钱。Kirkus World 管理着几十亿几十亿美元，是一家宏观对冲基金，跌了 6.4%，这是他们开始交易以来最大的单月跌幅。Chris Rokos 是另一位传奇的宏观对冲基金经理，我们今天刚报道，他上个月亏了近 5%。所以上个月这个市场里真的无处可藏。

turns.en: Earlier this year, We did a live show of Odd Lots. And Torsen Slok from Apollo, we had him deliver his slides. His favorite charts of the time.
turns.zh: 今年早些时候，我们做过一场 Odd Lots 现场秀，请到了 Apollo 的 Torsten Slok 展示他的幻灯片，他最喜欢的图表。

turns.en: The king of charts.
turns.zh: 图表之王。

turns.en: The king of charts, Torsen Slok from Apollo. And his basic thesis is that the market has emerged... into there's the AI factor and then there's the anti-AI factor. And maybe you can't hide because everything is implicitly this trade one way or another. When you look at the results, do you come to the same conclusion that whether you're talking about a macro fund, whether you're talking about a sort of traditional long short, whether you're talking about a single manager, whether you're talking about a strategic one, that at the end of the day, if you had been making money in this market, prior to October or maybe prior to June or whatever, that you had been making money implicitly via long AI?
turns.zh: 图表之王，Apollo 的 Torsten Slok。他的基本论点是：市场已经分裂成"AI 因子"和"反 AI 因子"两块。也许你根本无处可藏，因为一切都在以某种方式隐性地做着这笔交易。你看到这些业绩结果之后，会不会得出同样的结论——不管你讲的是宏观基金、传统多空、单一经理，还是策略型基金——归根结底，如果你在 10 月之前，或者 6 月之前，在这个市场里赚到过钱，那你其实就是通过隐性做多 AI 赚的？

turns.en: Well, if that is the measure, then I don't know who is anti-AI because I don't see many winners here for the whole.
turns.zh: 如果这就是衡量标准，那我真不知道谁是"反 AI"的，因为我在这整个……

turns.en: Industry as a whole.
turns.zh: 整个行业里，都没看到多少赢家。

turns.en: There might be some exceptions, but it doesn't seem to be an equal split or even maybe it 25, 75. It looks like the entire industry has piled into this AI theme, maybe not directly through stocks, but maybe they have exposure to credit that has exposure to AI, or maybe AI has started to impact macro. started to impact interest rates.
turns.zh: 也许有一些例外，但看起来并不是五五开，甚至可能也不是二八开——倒像是整个行业都挤进了这个 AI 主题。也许不是直接通过股票，但可能是通过有 AI 敞口的信用债，或者是 AI 已经开始影响宏观、开始影响利率。

turns.en: Yeah, I was just going to say short treasuries could be an AI trade or a long AI trade, right? Yeah.
turns.zh: 对，我正想说，做空国债也可以是一笔 AI 交易，或者是做多 AI 的交易，对吧？是的。

turns.en: Well, actually, on this note, we did get a really interesting report. We do have some analysis that we can look at to get clues of what these funds were actually doing. So Pivotal Path put out this report last week saying that hedge funds were basically all crowding into the same names, which again, for multistrats at least, was exactly what you were supposed to not see. They were supposed to be diversified and making all these independent bets. Talk to us about what Pivotal Path actually found.
turns.zh: 说到这里，我们确实拿到了一份很有意思的报告，有一些分析可以帮我们找到线索，看看这些基金到底在做什么。PivotalPath 上周发布了一份报告，说对冲基金基本上都挤在同样的股票上——这对多策略基金来说，恰恰是本来最不该出现的现象。它们本该分散化、彼此独立地下注。跟我们说说 PivotalPath 到底发现了什么。

turns.en: So mainly they were arguing for crowded trades. That was my reading. And I will separate it from momentum and everything. You can like have 10 very sophisticated hedge funds independently deciding they like the same stock, perhaps because they're liquid or maybe the earnings are strong or Maybe it fits in their risk framework. That doesn't make them momentum traders, but it does create this problem that if they all change their mind at the same time, which seems to have what has happened maybe last month, then it's a big problem. So Pivotal Path says the 10 largest firms it studied control about $ 2. 2 trillion, including borrowed money. That is a massive amount of money. And the capital backing that trade was something like $ 300 and $ 350 billion. That gives you a sense of how much leverage is in the system. So the report itself doesn't predict stress. But if you look at another report, which is from Goldman, The broader work they have done shows that correlations between multi-strategy funds themselves have strayed roughly 0.2, 0.3 band for years. So that doesn't point to maybe too much correlation, but crowding has become a big issue and it's backed by huge amounts of leveraged. And then it's concentrated in this tiny little world or maybe not tiny after anthropic IPO. tiny world of AI stocks. So when one thing's cracked, it leads to like the flood of problems for hedge funds. And that's what happened last month.
turns.zh: 主要是说存在拥挤交易，这是我读到的重点。我把它和动量之类的东西分开来看。你可以有 10 家非常老练的对冲基金，各自独立地决定喜欢同一只股票，也许是因为流动性好，也许是因为盈利强劲，也许是因为它符合各自的风险框架。这并不使他们成为动量交易者，但确实会造成一个问题——如果他们同时改变主意（这似乎就是上个月发生的事），那就是大麻烦。PivotalPath 说，它研究的最大 10 家公司控制了大约 2.2 万亿美元（包括借来的钱），这是巨量的钱。支撑这些交易的资本大约在 3000 亿到 3500 亿美元之间，你就能感受到系统里有多少杠杆。这份报告本身并没有预测压力，但如果你看另一份来自 Goldman 的报告——他们做过的更广的研究显示，多策略基金之间的相关性多年来一直在 0.2 到 0.3 这个区间浮动。所以这并不一定意味着相关性过高，但拥挤已经成了大问题，而且背后有巨量杠杆支撑。然后这一切又集中在这个小小的 AI 股票世界里——Anthropic IPO 之后也许就不算小了。所以当有一处裂开，就引发对冲基金的一连串问题，这就是上个月发生的事。

turns.en: So just on the leverage point, when a fund's positions start to go down, and I'm particularly interested in multi-strats here, but we can talk about funds in general too. When positions start to go down, What happens next? Is it like the portfolio manager decides to start cutting risk, or the centralized risk management team says you have to cut back on risk, or you have a volatility model that says you need to trim down exposure, or in some famous cases recently, does the prime broker start asking for more collateral and so you're forced to start liquidating positions?
turns.zh: 就说杠杆这一点——当一只基金的仓位开始下跌时（我尤其关心多策略基金，但也可以聊一般基金），接下来会发生什么？是组合经理自己决定开始削减风险，还是中央风控团队说你必须削减风险，还是有一个波动率模型告诉你需要压缩敞口，或者像最近几个著名的例子那样，主经纪商开始要求更多抵押品，于是你被迫开始平仓？

turns.en: Yes, so let's look at this multi-strat model. In a way, they are the real hedge fund industry right now. Everything connects to them. The way I think about Multistrat is they are like a hedge fund supermarket. Instead of one star manager making all the decisions, you have these hundreds of individual portfolio managers or what we call pods. Trading different things. So one team may be trading U.S. stocks, another macro, another trading credit commodities, and so on and so forth. And sitting above all of that is a very powerful risk management machine. At most of the, at all the hedge funds, like this is the key. The firm decides how much capital each PM gets, how much they can lose, how much leverage they can use. how much risk the whole platform wants. If a PM loses money, risk gets cut. So for example, if you have $ 100 to manage and if you lose 5% of that, so $ 5, at many of the firms, your capital will be cut into half. If you lose another 2.5%, so total loss becoming 7.5%, you are closed out. You can be liquidated and you can get fired immediately. And that's why this is a very ruthless risk management arrangement that multi-strats have. And that's what makes them wonderful in a way. This ruthlessness makes the machine work really well because they don't allow you to lose so much that you become a problem for the whole hedge fund. If the losses continue, the allocation can disappear and obviously eventually the portfolio manager. The theory here really is that lots of relatively small uncorrelated return streams are more robust than like one gigantic star portfolio manager putting on a bet. So you are avoiding the key man risk. Like a star manager can make you really, really insanely rich. But if he gets it wrong, he has the ability to also destroy your machine altogether.
turns.zh: 是的，我们来看多策略这个模式。某种意义上，他们才是当下真正的对冲基金行业，所有东西都和他们挂钩。我对多策略的理解是——他们像一家对冲基金超市。不是一位明星经理做所有决策，而是有几百个独立的组合经理（我们称为 pod），各自交易不同的东西：一个团队做美股，一个做宏观，一个做信用，一个做商品，等等等等。而在这之上，是一个非常强大的风控机器。所有这类对冲基金里，这一点是关键——公司决定每个 PM 拿到多少资本、能承受多少亏损、能用多少杠杆、整个平台愿意承担多少风险。如果一个 PM 亏钱，风险就被砍掉。举个例子，如果你手里有 100 美元可以管，亏了 5%（也就是 5 美元），在很多这类公司里，你的资本就会被砍掉一半。再亏 2.5%（累计亏 7.5%），你就被清盘了，可能被立刻炒掉。所以这是一种非常无情的风控安排——这也正是多策略的"美妙之处"。这种无情让机器运转得非常好，因为他们不允许你亏到成为整个对冲基金的问题。如果亏损继续，配额可以消失，最后 PM 本人也会消失。这里的核心理论是：许多相对小规模、不相关的收益流，比一位巨大的明星 PM 押一笔大注要更稳健。这样你就避免了"关键人物风险"（key man risk）。明星经理能让你变得超级有钱，但如果他做错，他也有能力把你的整台机器一起毁掉。

turns.en: So as you said, They're very, okay, there's this AI trade, but there's various flavors of how you can express bullishness on AI. And so let's say I'm the risk manager at one of these and Tracy is sort of long chips or maybe long memory.
turns.zh: 就像你说的，他们非常——好，有这笔 AI 交易，但表达看多 AI 的方式有很多种。假设我是其中一家公司的风控主管，Tracy 大概在做多芯片，或者做多存储器。

turns.en: I would never, go on.
turns.zh: 我才不会呢。你继续说。

turns.en: And Nishant, you're like short treasuries because you think there's gonna be a lot of CapEx and that's gonna drive inflation, et cetera. Isn't it my job to say like, yes, they're actually making the same trade. This is not diversification. And so it's like, yeah, maybe I'll fire both of you. But isn't it for having a bad month because treasuries have rallied a lot over the last few weeks. But isn't it my fault for not having identified the fact that you are not giving me diversification. You are all making the same trade in different skins.
turns.zh: 而 Nishant，你在做空国债，因为你觉得会有大量资本开支（CapEx），会推高通胀等等。难道我的职责不就是指出——是的，他们其实是在做同一笔交易，这不是分散化。所以我或许会想，那就把你们两个都开了吧。但并不是因为你们这个月表现差——毕竟国债最近几周涨了那么多——难道不是我的失职吗？我没有识别出你们根本没给我分散化，你们只是在用不同的皮做同一笔交易。

turns.en: Well, have you seen any risk manager fire him?
turns.zh: 那你有没有看到哪位风控主管真的开除过谁？

turns.en: I don't know. Do you ever hear, is that a thing? But shouldn't, if I have a lot of PMs making correlated bets, isn't it my fault?
turns.zh: 我不知道。你听说过这种事吗？这算不算一个普遍现象？但如果我手下有很多 PM 在做相关联的下注，难道不是我的错吗？

turns.en: Well, the beauty of correlation is that it's not visible all the time. It goes up and down. And in moments like last month, it really goes up. So that interconnectedness, the impact of leveraging the system, how everyone is positioned, it's a very complex mathematics, I think. And it's a complex job. Plus, you can't rule it out. If you see, you know, Mac 7 and all these tech stops going so much. And if you, as a risk manager, come in and say that, okay, let's cut it out. And if you underperform, that's a very hard decision to make. And that's where some of these multistrat, I mean, to be precise, I mean, they are great at it. They do care about correlation and they do manage it. But eventually, if everything falls together, and it's not that everything fell together. It was first, it was AI. Then you sort of kind of rebalance your portfolio that the bonds go down. Then the problem in the credit market is, than Brazil. So it happened week after week after week. So that's where I think all the problems started to emerge.
turns.zh: 相关性这东西的"美妙"之处就在于，它并不总是可见的，它上下波动。像上个月那种时刻，它就真的飙升。所以那种相互关联、系统里的杠杆影响、每个人的仓位分布——我觉得这是非常复杂的数学，也是非常复杂的工作。而且你不能排除这种情况：如果你看到 Mag 7 和这些科技股涨那么多，作为风控主管你说"好了，砍掉吧"，然后如果你砍掉之后表现落后，那是一个非常难做的决定。这就是为什么我觉得一些多策略——准确地说，他们其实很擅长这件事，他们确实在意相关性并且管理它。但最终，如果所有东西一起下跌——而且并不是所有东西"一起"跌的：先是 AI，然后你稍微再平衡一下组合，债券又开始跌；然后信用市场出问题；然后是巴西。所以是一周接一周接一周地发生。我觉得所有的问题就是这样开始浮现的。

turns.en: Well, I still remember we did that episode with Krishna Kumar about multi-strats. This was one of the first episodes. we ever did about multi-strats. And his characterization of the funds was that they're not maximizing for long-term returns, they're maximizing for short-term returns. So like every macro event that happens or every move, they react to it very quickly, right? And so when you have a succession of all these idiosyncratic things happening, You could see them sort of cutting positions. I think they cut AI exposure going into the midterms, but then the market started rallying on Wednesday. And so they went back in and then it falls on like Friday.
turns.zh: 我还记得我们做过一期节目，请了 Krishna Kumar 聊多策略基金，那是我们最早做多策略的节目之一。他对这些基金的刻画是：它们不是在最大化长期回报，而是在最大化短期回报。所以每有一个宏观事件、每一次波动，他们都非常快地做出反应，对吧？所以当这些特异性的事情一件接一件发生时，你会看到他们在不断砍仓。我记得他们在中期选举之前砍掉了 AI 敞口，但周三市场又开始反弹，于是他们又杀回去，然后周五又跌。

turns.en: And Thursday was the day they got a really.
turns.zh: 周四是他们真的……的那一天。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And so they're just like reacting very strongly to each new day, which I think has posed a problem, certainly in recent weeks. So on that note, what do we need to see? To know that the multistrats are like piling back into the market or that leverage limits or exposure limits are starting to go up and they're able to take on risk again.
turns.zh: 所以他们对每一个新的一天都在非常强烈地做反应，我觉得这在最近几周确实造成了问题。那么，我们需要看到什么，才能知道多策略基金在重新入场，或者杠杆限额、敞口限额开始上调，他们可以重新承担风险了？

turns.en: Well, there are many statistics in the market and banks are in the best position to see that. But this week, things have already recovered a lot, it seems. There is already mean reversion. There is buying the dip, it seems. But the problem is we are in November and 10 days are gone and a lot of these portfolios are bleeding. On top of that, talking to people, the anecdotal evidence I see is that dozens and dozens of portfolio managers, big risk takers in equity space, in macro space, in credit space, they have been fired or they have been poached by others or they are spending their long non-competes on the beach. So there are a lot of people who are not in the market and we are in November, just 40 more days left for this year. Do they have courage to get into this market and take risk and make the most out of the next one and a half months? That is the question. And at the same time, not so many people are out of this market. So, Next two months is going to be very, very, very difficult. You know, what will it take traders to take risk now? And if they are wrong, you know, already bad performance can become so worse that they will lose their job anyways.
turns.zh: 市场上有很多统计数据，银行处在最好的位置去看这些。但这周情况看起来已经恢复了不少，均值回归（mean reversion）已经出现，看起来在逢低买入。但问题是，我们已经进入 11 月，10 天过去了，很多组合还在流血。除此之外，我和业内人聊下来得到的轶事证据是——几十位组合经理、股票方面的大风险承担者、宏观、信用方面的大风险承担者，已经被开除，或者被别人挖走，或者在海滩上度过他们长长的竞业禁止期（non-compete）。所以有很多人已经不在市场里了，而我们才刚进 11 月，今年只剩 40 多天。他们有没有勇气重新进入这个市场、承担风险、把接下来这一个半月榨出最大的收益？这是问题所在。同时，市场外的人并不多。所以接下来两个月会非常非常非常艰难。要让交易者现在承担风险，需要什么？如果他们错了，本来就已经糟糕的业绩会变得糟糕到他们无论如何都会失业。

Setting aside the performance of October, and this is an industry-related question, but setting aside the performance of October, you've just been hearing a lot about sort of like how many more multi-strats or variations on a theme are really necessary for How many more launches can we have that roughly either try to replicate the Citadel model or the Millennium model or whatever it is? Where do we stand with this? Like, in your view, is this just sort of saturated, especially when you consider the cost of, say, acquiring new talent? So, again, in my imaginary world, I want to launch a new Multistrat. I'm going to have to pay up to higher season traders that know what they're doing. turns.zh: 这个不错，我觉得会很受欢迎，我非常喜欢这个主意。Nishant，我最后一个问题。撇开 10 月的业绩不谈——这是一个跟行业相关的问题——撇开 10 月的业绩，你最近肯定听到很多讨论说：到底还需要多少家多策略基金、或者多少家主题变体？我们还能再上多少个基本上在复制 Citadel 模式、Millennium 模式之类的新基金？现在这个行业处在什么位置？在你看来，它是不是已经饱和了，尤其考虑到获取新人才的成本？还是在我的假想世界里，我要新成立一家多策略基金，就得付高价从别处挖来那些真正懂行的交易者。所以你觉得，这个行业现在打到第几局了？

turns.en: So we have already seen the problems in the multistrat industry in terms of starting a new multistrat. We saw at Jane Global, we saw at Walleye cutting parts of their equities trading. We have seen Eisler shutting down. So that's one side of the story. But in terms of demand for these strategies? Why do we need another multi-strategy hedge fund? Or why do anyone try to launch a new multi-strategy hedge fund? Because investors really want this strategy.
turns.zh: 我们已经看到了多策略行业里新起基金的一些问题：Jane Global 的问题、Walleye 砍掉部分股票交易、Eisler 关停。这是一方面。但对这类策略的需求方面——为什么我们还需要另一家多策略对冲基金？为什么有人还要去创立新的多策略对冲基金？因为投资人真的想要这个策略。

turns.en: It lets you run more money, right? Like the more pods you add, the more money you get to run.
turns.zh: 它能让你管更多的钱，对吧？你 pod 加得越多，你能管的钱就越多。

turns.en: You can, you can, but there is a limit to that. Like how many ways, if you already have like dozens and dozens of equity portfolio managers, How much an incremental or additional five more equity fund management will diversify your strategy? So I think there is a cap on that as well. So investors want it. They can't deploy enough capital to these multi-strategy hedge funds. If you look at the top players, all of them are close to new money. One example which shows you how hot these hedge funds are Millennium wanted to raise about $ 20 billion in new capital earlier this year. They got demand for more than $ 30 billion. They took in $ 22 billion. I don't think more than 2% of the hedge fund industry, or even 1% of the hedge fund industry by number, managed $ 20 billion. So that's the kind of demand that these hedge funds have. At the same time, many of these large players are returning capital. Between D, Shaw, Point72, and Citadel, almost $ 35- 40 billion have been returned to investors. Now those investors need to find a new home for this capital. Where do they put in? This is a $ 40 billion problem for investors. So capacity is a real issue. If someone can genuinely build a multistrat and create decent capacity, with reasonable returns, there is demand for another multistrat. The question whether someone can build it or not is very tough to answer. We have seen many failed attempts. And that is the problem. Whether a new hedge fund, multistrategy hedge fund, has the right and resources to sort of employ another or poach another trader and hire the best people, that is the big question. I don't think they can.
turns.zh: 可以，可以，但这有上限。如果你已经有几十位股票组合经理，那再多请五位股票基金经理，对你的策略分散化能有多少帮助？所以这方面也有天花板。投资人想要，但他们没法把足够多的钱投进这些多策略基金。看看头部玩家，他们几乎都对新资金关着门。举个例子说明这些对冲基金有多火：Millennium 今年早些时候想募集大约 200 亿美元新资本，结果需求超过 300 亿美元，他们最终收了 220 亿。整个对冲基金行业里，能管 200 亿美元的公司，我觉得连 2% 都不到，甚至可能连 1% 都不到（按公司数量算）。这就是这些对冲基金面对的需求。同时，很多头部玩家在退还资本。D. E. Shaw、Point72、Citadel 加起来，几乎有 350 亿到 400 亿美元被退还给投资人。现在这些投资人得给这笔钱找新家，能放哪儿？这是投资人面临的一个 400 亿美元的难题。所以容量真的是个问题。如果有人能真正建起一家多策略，做出像样的容量、有合理的回报，市场对新的多策略基金是有需求的。但能不能建起来，这个问题非常难回答，我们已经见过很多失败的尝试，这就是问题所在。一家新的多策略对冲基金有没有资源和权利去挖另一位交易者、请到最优秀的人，这才是大问题。我不觉得他们能做到。

turns.en: Yeah, I think the obvious takeaway from this is that more teams, more pods, more money does not necessarily translate into more adjusted returns, basically. All right, Nishant, thank you so much for coming on All Thoughts. Really appreciate it. We'll let you get back to reporting because there's probably eight stories that you need to write today.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这里面一个显而易见的启示是：更多的团队、更多的 pod、更多的钱，并不必然转化为更高的风险调整后回报。好了，Nishant，非常感谢你来 OddLots，真的很感谢。我们放你回去继续报道，因为你今天可能还有八条稿子要写。

turns.en: Thank you. All right.
turns.zh: 谢谢。好的。

turns.en: Well, that was our conversation, Nishant Kumar. And now let's talk a little bit more about the markets. We have here Michael Ball, macro strategist at Bloomberg News. He's going to explain to us all these big moves. Michael, thanks for coming on the pod. First time, I think, right?
turns.zh: 好，这就是我们和 Nishant Kumar 的对话。现在我们来多聊一下市场。我们请到了 Bloomberg News 的宏观策略师 Michael Ball，他会给我们解释所有这些大波动。Michael，感谢上我们的节目，我记得这是你第一次上，对吧？

turns.zh: 第一次。谢谢你们邀请，非常荣幸。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: So this is the big question, right? So people expected a strong fall. turnout for the Dems in the midterm elections.
turns.zh: 这就是大问题，对吧？大家预期民主党在中期选举中会有很高的投票率。

turns.en: Right.

turns.en: I don't think a lot of people expected necessarily the blue tsunami, but it was leaning Dem for sure. And then on Wednesday, the market reaction was pretty muted. We saw, you know, stocks actually go up. And then Thursday, everyone seemed to just like wake up and decide that was entirely wrong. What happened? What were people thinking?

It would be better free cash flow, and hence their core businesses would do better. And here we go. The thing that had been driving their earnings growth was now a negative, and the things that were kind of more tangential were just on the side. So it was a super interesting setup Wednesday into Thursday. And again, Thursday, we didn't have a necessary catalyst. We had our standard micro stories with some AI headwinds. Semis and sort of AI trade on Wednesday had been weak. They had been underperforming. The rotation was back in. We saw equal weight outperforming. We saw value doing well. But then lo and behold, Thursday happened. And what happened was once we started breaking levels on the SPX, and this is the NASDAQ was already sort of in correction territory. We'd already had a big negative gamma backdrop, something I can talk about more, which was basically people were positioned defensively. But SPX was still hanging in there and we were above this sort of 7,700 level, 7,600 level, a range we'd been in for several months. This rotation that had occurred over the last few months had buffered the weakness we'd seen sort of in the AI trade in October. And subsequently that all sort of fell apart as levels broke and feeding became self-feeding, actually started, the weakness became self-feeding.
turns.zh: 周三其实也很有意思，因为超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers）反而被买入，逻辑是——蓝色浪潮带来更多监管，加上选票上还有各种关于 AI 的倡议，会迫使他们削减资本开支（CapEx），这样自由现金流会更好，从而他们的核心业务会做得更好。所以你看，一直在推动他们盈利增长的东西，现在变成了负面因素，而那些相对边缘的东西反倒被搁在一边。所以周三到周四是一个非常有意思的铺垫。周四我们并没有明确的催化剂，还是那些老套的微观故事加上一些 AI 逆风。半导体和 AI 交易周三就已经很弱，跑输大盘，轮动（rotation）回来了，我们看到等权重指数跑赢，价值股表现好。但结果没想到，周四是这么走的。发生的事情是——一旦我们开始跌破 SPX 的关键点位（NASDAQ 已经进入回调区间），加上我们本来就处在一个巨大的负 gamma 背景中（这个我可以多讲一些），也就是说大家仓位都偏防御性，但 SPX 还在撑着，还在 7700、7600 那个我们横了好几个月的区间之上。过去几个月发生的这种轮动，缓冲了 10 月 AI 交易的疲软。而随后一旦关键点位被跌破，跌势就变成了自我强化（self-feeding）。

turns.en: This is where the sort of like automatic mechanics of markets come into play. So the idea that like dealers have to cut positions just because they're breaking key levels, just because they need to maintain like a certain volatility weight and things like that.
turns.zh: 这就是市场的自动机制开始起作用的地方。也就是说，做市商必须砍仓，仅仅因为跌破了关键点位，仅仅因为他们需要维持某个波动率权重之类的。

So what happened here is that basically Legacy Eye calls some of these auto callables, some of these exotic products that you guys have actually talked about.

turns.en: Yeah. So there was, like, a clearing event basically in July. And August was a rebuild. And what all this meant was that RealizeVol got sort of suppressed because the way volatility works is it's supply and demand as well. Obviously, you want to think about buying and selling, driving it. But it's a little more complicated because on the other side, there's a backdrop in option markets, which supplies basically delta and gamma into the market, which is a fancy way of saying vol suppression or vol acceleration. So when people talk about gamma, what they often mean is where the dealers are holding option positioning. Are they long or short options? And effectively, if they're long options, they suppress volatility. And if they're short options, they accelerate the move. So I want to buy a put. I want downside protection. The dealer is short that put. So that Delta hedge that as the market goes down, they are selling into the market, which exacerbates that move, which is exactly what happened Thursday. On top of all these other kind of, you know, cross currents, we had obviously some hedge fund news that they were blowing up. People were getting taps on the shoulder. We had sort of leveraged ETFs accelerating that because that's a big market and that has to exacerbate the move as well. That's a negative convexity product. And then all of a sudden the vol control community and some of these systematic guys who are always the boogeyman that get blamed, but were actually quite active on Thursday. had to jump in because if volatility picks up, they have to de-gross. And even with sort of the CTAs being more neutral, that's another kind of buzzword that's often thrown around when we see these big market moves. So they chase trends. They too, although they were somewhat less long, were also very active in selling. And that was a perfect storm Thursday that got us basically to break all the ranges we'd been in for months and test new lows.
turns.zh: 对。7 月基本就发生了一次出清事件（clearing event），8 月是重建。这意味着已实现波动率（Realized Vol）被压制了，因为波动率的机制其实也是供求关系——你自然想到的是买卖驱动它，但另一侧稍微复杂一点：期权市场有一个背景，它向市场供给 delta 和 gamma，说得更"花哨"一点，就是波动率抑制（vol suppression）或者波动率加速（vol acceleration）。所以当人们讲 gamma 的时候，通常是在讲做市商持有的期权头寸在哪里，他们是做多期权还是做空期权？简单说，如果他们做多期权，就抑制波动率；如果做空期权，就加速波动。假设我要买一个 put（看跌期权），我要下行保护，那做市商就是这个 put 的空方。所以他们做 delta 对冲时，市场下跌他们就得跟着卖，这就加剧了跌势——这正是周四发生的事情。在所有这些其他逆流之上，我们还看到对冲基金爆仓的消息，有人被拍肩膀（劝退），杠杆 ETF（leveraged ETFs）也在加速这个走势——那是一个很大的市场，也是负凸性（negative convexity）产品，一定会加剧下跌。然后突然间，波动率控制（vol control）那一拨人以及一些系统化交易者——他们总是被当作背锅的"魔王"，但周四确实非常活跃——不得不下场，因为如果波动率上升，他们必须降总敞口。即使是 CTA——那是另一个经常被扔出来解释大行情的术语——虽然他们的多头程度稍轻，但也非常活跃地在卖出。所以周四是一场完美风暴，让我们基本上跌破了横盘好几个月的所有区间，去测试新低。

turns.zh: 我觉得 10 月真的是资本开支叙事（CapEx narrative）发生转变的时候，突然之间它不再是增长引擎，而变成了融资问题、自由现金流问题，再加上"邻避主义"（nimbyism）和电力问题——即资本开支的实际执行。我们在收益率上也看到了这一点，因为突然间我们对收益率随油价怎么走出现了反转。油价还在慢慢往上，因为伊朗问题显然没有任何进展，但突然间我们又有了增长担忧——因为按叙事逻辑，明年 AI 资本开支会大幅下降，然后就基本没有增长了，因为 AI 资本开支一直是主要驱动力。我们看到 10 年期国债收益率和曲线走平，大家越来越担心增长。最后发生的是——NASDAQ 变得更负，人们开始买入保护（protection），不只是在单只 AI 股票上，还作为指数层面的对冲。

turns.zh: 数据是很亮眼的。我在尽可能深挖财报电话会——不仅是超大规模云厂商，也包括 neocloud，还有产业层面的"卖铲人"（pick and shovel）。大家的订单积压（backlog）都很惊人。IREN 的算力需求非常亮眼，那里的增长——当然，杠杆很重，逆风很多，对利率也非常敏感。但整体来说，当你看到 70% 的回撤时，我还是觉得故事被过度演绎了。当然，我是 Bloomberg 的宏观策略师 Ball，其他同事可能有别的看法，但看起来的确出现了显著的回撤，而现在仓位已经清理干净。

turns.zh: 还有，说到算力租户，回到我们和 Nishant 聊的多策略对冲基金话题——分散化似乎也是个问题吧？如果你所有的租户都以某种方式暴露在 AI 上——我猜他们大概都是。

And literally, I think the AI trade now has become bigger than the Anthropix and NVIDIA. And I get that NVIDIA is seen as central for the financing. Maybe the growth trajectory as far as the advancements of new chips and where they take kind of M & A and like how they expand in that sense will change if Jensen leaves. turns.zh: 我在这件事上反复摇摆。这显然是过去 24 小时——从周末消息爆出以来——我们所有人都在辩论的问题。说实话，我觉得现在这个 AI 交易已经变得比 Anthropic 和 NVIDIA 本身还大。我理解 NVIDIA 被视为融资的核心，但我也要反驳说——即便 CEO 换人，这一点也不会变。也许新芯片的研发轨迹、他们如何做并购、如何扩张，如果 Jensen 走了会变。但作为基石，我目前还没看到任何让我觉得它会动摇的东西。而且昨天其实主要是所有人被空头挤压、被迫回补 put 的痛苦交易（pain trade）。所以半导体和 AI 相关个股其他都涨这件事，更像是机械性的——这才应该是主线。从周三开始的这最近三四天，真的都是机械性的行情，而不是像很多人说的那样，AI 叙事发生了大转变。这只是我的看法。

turns.en: When you have all this new equity supply, I guess, coming into the market, would you expect to see that have an impact on other AI stocks?
turns.zh: 当这么多新的股票供给进入市场时，你会不会预期它会对其他 AI 股票产生影响？

turns.en: Yeah, I think so. And I think obviously people have to sort of rebalance. I think, too, there's two broader things. One, this year has been one of the first years where actual broader equity supply is no longer shrinking. Buybacks, as we know, were primarily being driven by hyperscovers, which free cash flow now has shrunk enough that that buyback pulse, at least for 27, is totally under question. And it's come off this year. And when you take employee compensation, it's even less. You know, we had three years there since basically 24 where equity supply was actually shrinking. So that was very good as you still had massive passive flow. coming from even outside the corporate buybacks. Now, to your point, like, yeah, it's going to crowd out. But with that said, like, it's $ 80 billion. It looks like that's kind of the number they're throwing around. I mean, SpaceX was absorbed well, and I'd say that was a more risky proposition in some ways, although we can debate that as well, and probably a higher valuation.
turns.zh: 对，我觉得会。而且显然大家必须重新平衡。我觉得还有两个更宏观的点：一是今年是最早几个"整体股票供给不再萎缩"的年份之一。我们知道，回购（buyback）此前主要是由超大规模云厂商驱动的，而现在他们的自由现金流已经萎缩到——至少对 2027 年来说——那个回购脉冲完全成了问号，而且今年已经下来了。加上员工股权激励（employee compensation），供给就更少了。从 2024 年基本开始，我们经历了三年股票供给实际在萎缩的时期，那时候非常好——即使不算公司回购，你还有大量被动资金流入。现在，就像你说的，会挤出其他标的。但话虽如此，也就是 800 亿美元左右——这看起来是他们放出来的数字。SpaceX 就被吸收得很好，我觉得那在某种意义上是风险更高的一个标的，虽然这个也可以争论，估值可能还更高。

turns.en: We don't need to debate that.
turns.zh: 这个我们不用争。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.zh: 但我想，看，这些数字理论上很大，可市场本身也很大，只要背后的故事够吸引人——我觉得是的——它就能吸收。而且现在估值已经下来了。如果是在 2 万亿美元那个水平，我可能会更担心。所以感觉像是——先熬过这次风险事件，然后进入故事的下一段。这就是我在"出清事件"上的位置。

turns.en: Can we talk about the hyperscalers themselves? I was thinking about this. Like if I think of a company like Alphabet. And meta, these are the two examples. There's a legacy business that prints money, and that is Search. And it is still a huge moneymaker. There is a capital intensive business, but is also quite profitable in unit economics, and that is building clouds, either for themselves or for others. turns.zh: 这当然决定了你想给不同业务板块分配什么样的估值倍数。我觉得有意思的地方是——超大规模云厂商表现不好，是因为他们的传统业务在挣扎。而且他们挣扎的原因在外部：Amazon 有些问题，Microsoft 有些问题，Google 有些问题——顺便说，Microsoft 其实做得还不错。但 Google 的搜索有些问题，这完全说得通，因为搜索疲软……我用 Claude 比用 Google 更多，可能这不利于 token 使用量。我不该这样，但我们都在学着适应这项新技术。这对搜索之类的传统业务来说，可能会有点紧张。所以这说得通，但我认为——回到你的问题——云业务的增长和货币化才是整个故事的基石。

turns.en: For investors, the number one question.
turns.zh: 对投资人来说，头号问题就是……

But as long as compute's growing, they can probably power their way through this. And that's what we're hearing. And when I look to some of the experts on the street, like the Gavin Bakers and these guys who put out quite a lot, it's really about watching that metric. And so far, there really isn't any flinch. We're still in a decent part of the S-curve there.
turns.zh: 算力 CapEx 必须继续增长，而它现在还在以相当亮眼的速度增长。这就是为什么我们全都陷入这些叙事——token 价格、融资、竞争、邻避主义。但只要算力还在增长，他们大概就能强行突破这一切。这也是我们听到的。当我看街上一些专家——比如 Gavin Baker 这些人，他们输出很多——重点其实都在盯这个指标。到目前为止，还没有任何退缩。我们仍然处在这条 S 曲线相当不错的一段。

turns.en: Yeah, it's big. And I mean, it's decoupled from rates again, which was nice. I mean, yesterday was interesting. That's Monday. effectively equities were ripping, yields were sort of rising because all of a sudden the growth picture was getting better and that traditional kind of balance between rates and equity had kind of resumed, but oil had fallen massively. And usually oil would drag down sort of yields and treasuries and we didn't get that. So people were again, re-changing sort of the calibration correlations across asset. I think JP Morgan upped their surplus for even this year to 1.5 million barrels. And the product market's actually loose and nice. So crack spreads and all that have come off. So the energy pulse, as we just saw in CPI today, had been materially starting to come into core, changing our Fed calculations. So anything now with oil falling down, and I don't know where the range is because there'll be a higher premium and there's still a lot of inventory to be rebuilt. And there's still obviously a lot of things lurking with not only the Gulf, but Ukraine and Russia, which could change some of that. But the price will be higher, but it looks like now the skew is funny enough lower, although it'll be a bumpy path because again, now we're a little bit oversold. We just moved about $ 10, $ 15 in a short amount of period. Our size are oversold. Option position, funny enough, yesterday picked up. People were buying calls again. You could see $ 100. Dollar Brent being kind of a point where people thought we'd get back to.
turns.zh: 是的，很重要。而且它跟利率再度脱钩了，这挺好的。我是说，昨天很有意思——那是周一——股票大涨，收益率在上行，因为突然间增长前景变好了，那种利率和股票之间的传统平衡又恢复了。但油价却大幅下跌，通常油价会把收益率和国债往下拽，但这次没有。所以大家在重新校准跨资产的相关性。但就石油本身来说，如果我们能结束这种地缘政治风险溢价（geopolitical risk premium）的压制，其实背景是正面的。桶数正在出来，我记得 JP Morgan 把今年的过剩量上调到了 150 万桶。成品油市场其实很宽松，很好——裂解价差（crack spread）之类都下来了。即使在欧洲，比如荷兰天然气市场也降了不少，帮助了欧洲股票。所以能源脉冲——正如我们今天在 CPI 里看到的——已经开始实质性地进入核心通胀，改变我们对 Fed 的计算。所以现在油价下跌的话——我也不知道区间在哪里，因为溢价会更高，而且还有大量库存需要重建，显然波斯湾之外还有乌克兰和俄罗斯的问题潜伏着，可能会改变一些东西——但价格会更高。不过有意思的是，偏度（skew）反倒更低了，虽然路径会很颠簸，因为我们现在有点超卖，短期内油价大概跌了 10 到 15 美元。RSI 超卖。期权仓位反倒昨天上升了——人们又开始买 call。你可以看到 100 美元的 Brent 是大家觉得会回到的一个点。

turns.zh: 谢谢。Joe，我觉得这是对当下情况一个非常好的梳理。对我来说，上周就是市场机制（mechanics of markets）的全面展示。再说一次，我们做了这么多期关于结构化产品、多策略基金、杠杆 ETF 之类的节目，原因就是——你确实会看到，一旦市场开始下跌，它们会加剧波动率、加剧抛压，我觉得上周就是这种情况。而且再回到多策略，我觉得这给它们的商业模式打上了一个大大的问号，尤其是多策略基金的核心特征——聚焦短期回报。所以当外部环境每天都在翻转，他们在追赶趋势、或者对趋势做出反应的时候，就会加剧卖出或者买入的力量。
